fair_value_reason: P/E leg (0.6): 11x FY28 EPS of about $8.10 = $89.1. FCF leg (0.4): $1.0B FCF at a 10% EV yield = $10.0B, plus about $1.35B net cash, over about 126M Sep-2027 shares = $90.1. Blend $89.5, plus about $0.45 one-off net tariff refund, about $90. This equals the agent mean ($89.8). It is up $1 from my round-1 $89 because FY27 consensus ($7.52) already sits above the guide top on cheaper buybacks. agent_4's 11.5x (+$4) and agent_3's $7.80 EPS (-$3) are the main outliers and roughly offset.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged on a fair value of about $90 (range $87-92) and a median near $83, but the convergence is mostly the agents adopting my round-1 numbers. The real fact corrections underneath (136.4M shares falling to about 126M, ~$1.0B FCF verified in XBRL, the Skechers multiple being a take-private) are sound. I settle FY28 EPS at about $8.10, 11x and net cash at about $1.35B for a $90 fair value, equal to the agent mean. The new Wells Fargo GLP-1 Underweight is real but five months old and priced (PT $85 is above spot). The only ladder change is a modest widening of both tails to match 44.5% realized vol. Near term, Nike reports tonight (Oct 1) and DECK's Q2, probably Oct 22, is the binary that decides whether HOKA's H2 acceleration holds.
key_drivers: HOKA US: Q1 HOKA wholesale +2.9% and domestic +3.2% vs DTC +17.3%, and segment op income +0.8%. Q2 (~Oct 22) must show the guided H2 international-wholesale step-up or the FY27 guide is at risk (BMO).
Per-share compounding: 136.41M shares (Jul-9) to about 126M by Sep-2027 at about 80% of ~$1.0B FCF near $80-88. That carries FY28 EPS to about $8.0-8.1 even on flat net income.
Multiple regime: about 9.9x NTM today, and 11x FY28 at the horizon is about 10.3x NTM. Base rates (Crocs 7-9x for years) say re-rating is rare, so returns come from EPS and buybacks.
UGG holiday quarter (Q3 FY27, late January), the largest EPS quarter, with a full 12.5% tariff impact.
Sentiment and momentum: the stock is -23% year on year and -20% since Aug 7, with two Underweights (BMO PT $70, Wells Fargo GLP-1 PT $85). The bar into Q2 is low, but momentum is negative.
